title.narrative: Emergency response to support returnees and vulnerable population in Afar region with integrated health services including SRH, Nutrition, GBV and MHPSS

description.narrative:
ltpgtltspangtltspangtThe main aim of this initiative is to reduce the morbidity and mortality rates among the targeted communities affected by crises in the Afar region of Ethiopia, including Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), returnees, and vulnerable host populations. MdM and the partner organization - Afar Pastoralist Development Association (APDA), strategic focus is on improving healthcare services within the region, with a particular emphasis on the Teru woreda where displaced populations have returned to their original areas. The project will support 2 health centers (HCs) and 3 Health Posts (HPs) currently accessible in this region and will reach 26,877 beneficiaries with 700,000$. The project is designed to offer a comprehensive primary healthcare services, encompassing Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH), Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS), Gender-Based Violence (GBV) response, and Nutrition services. Additionally, the project will prioritize extensive engagement with the community to raise awareness and encourage the utilization of these vital healthcare facilities. For those facing difficulties accessing functioning healthcare facilities, we will deploy Mobile Health and Nutrition Teams (MNHT) to provide a basic package of medical services. Our focus will include SRH such as Basic Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care (BEmONC), Family planning, MHPSS counseling services, GBV case management and medical support for survivors of Sexual and Gender-Based Violence (SGBV). Furthermore, our project will support early identification through MUAC screening and provide treatment for malnutrition for children under five years old (CU-5). To strengthen the capacity of the HCs and HPs, MDM will provide comprehensive support, including healthcare worker training, the provision of medications and medical equipment, and Long-Lasting Insecticide Nets (LLINs), IPC measures to create a safer and more hygienic environment for both healthcare workers and patients, and equipment to meet the required safety standards for medical activities. The project will ensure minor renovations on existing facilities and equipping the targeted facilities to be gender and disability sensitive. In our commitment to maintaining high healthcare standards, we will focus on strengthening infection prevention and control measures at the supported HCs and HPs. To ensure quality of health intervention, project will realize comprehensive technical trainings e.g. BEmONC, Community-based Management of Acute Malnutrition (CMAM), and Clinical Management of Rape whereas training for Psychological First Aid (PFA), GBV case management will be conducted through other funding. for health workers and community volunteers. The proposed project will identify and reinforce existing referral pathways to ensure survivors receive timely and appropriate care. Moreover, our project places great importance on being prepared for emergencies. We understand the importance of collaboration across sectors to comprehensively address the complex needs of the affected population. Therefore, we will actively engage and coordinate with other humanitarian organizations, government agencies, and local partners to ensure a cohesive and efficient response covering various sectors, including health, nutrition, protection, etc. Our exit strategy is based on the principle of sustainability. We will closely work with local authorities, community leaders, and partner organizations to enhance local capacity and ownership of the healthcare services provided. This will include training and mentoring of local healthcare workers and strengthening of the community health systems to ensure the continuation of essential services beyond the project's duration. We will also facilitate the transfer of knowledge and skills to local counterparts, enabling them to independently manage and sustain the healthcare initiatives implemented under this project, thus making a lasting impact on the communities we serve.lt/spangt
